unresolved.what: CRECUST RUN TRANSID(WS-RUN-TRANSID) → which programs run
unresolved.why: The transaction IDs are computed in a loop (expected: OCR1–OCR5, by constant evaluation). Which program each transaction runs is a CICS resource definition (CSD), which is not in the repository. The pairing OCRn → CRDTAGYn is suggested by the names only and must be reported as unresolved, not asserted.

The facility type is set at run time by EXEC CICS INQUIRE ASSOCIATION, so whether the debit checks apply to a given request can't be decided from source. The program's own comment (DBCRFUN, 'COMM-FACILTYPE(496 = NONE)') is documentation, not a proven value.

unresolved.what: ABNDPROC WRITE FILE(ABNDFILE): the file's organization
unresolved.why: A CICS file; whether it is a VSAM KSDS is defined in the CSD and the dataset definitions, not in the repository.
Calls through procedure pointers to the Java Native Interface (COBOL–Java interop), not COBOL programs. They must be classified as JNI calls, not resolved or reported as missing programs.

rules.title: A teller debit is refused when it would take the available balance below zero (the overdraft limit is read but not applied)

input.note: a '-' sign on the screen makes the amount a debit

decision.note: reads the account row, including AVAILABLE_BALANCE and OVERDRAFT_LIMIT

outcome.text: STRING 'Sorry insufficient funds available to pro'

rules.also: Related: a payment out of a MORTGAGE or LOAN account sets fail code 4 (DBCRFUN 330–335), which BNK1CRA has no message for (it falls to WHEN OTHER, 'the AMOUNT could not be applied').

rules.title: A customer may hold at most ten accounts: an eleventh is refused

input.note: the create-account screen links to CREACC

decision.note: the customer must exist (INQCUST); otherwise fail code 1
the customer's accounts are listed by INQACCCU

rules.also: The same program refuses account types other than ISA, MORTGAGE, SAVING, CURRENT and LOAN (ACCOUNT-TYPE-CHECK, CREACC 1303 onward).

rules.title: A new customer's credit score is the average of the agency scores that arrive in time, and 0 if none do

input.note: the create-customer screen links to CRECUST

decision.note: each agency returns a score from 1 to 999 (random in this sample)

outcome.note: the customer row is inserted with the score

condition.score: sum of received scores / number received
condition.fallback: 0 when no agency replies in time

rules.note: The agencies are deliberately dummies (random delay 0–3 s, random score). The rule worth extracting is the aggregation and its fallbacks, not the agencies' scores.

golden_trace.question: When a teller debits an account, what decides whether it is refused, and what does the teller see?

steps.what: The teller enters an account number and an amount with a sign on the BNK1CRA screen; '-' makes it a debit
BNK1CRA asks CICS where the request came from (facility type, at run time)
BNK1CRA links to DBCRFUN with its own layout of the parameters (SUBPGM-PARMS, 92 bytes)
DBCRFUN receives them through the PAYDBCR copybook (132 bytes)
DBCRFUN reads the account's balances and limits from DB2
A debit (amount below zero) from a MORTGAGE or LOAN account is refused with code 4
Otherwise, if the available balance plus the (negative) amount is below zero, it is refused with code 3; the overdraft limit is not used
On success DBCRFUN updates the balances and records the transaction in PROCTRAN
BNK1CRA reads the outcome and shows the teller a message

evidence.text: STRING 'Sorry insufficient funds available to pro'
MOVE 'Amount successfully applied to the account.' TO

lineage: screen AMTI + SIGNI → BNK1CRA.WS-AMOUNT-AS-FLOAT → BNK1CRA.SUBPGM-AMT (offset 8, 12 bytes)
DBCRFUN.COMM-SUCCESS / COMM-FAIL-CODE (offsets 130, 131) → BNK1CRA.SUBPGM-SUCCESS / SUBPGM-FAIL-CODE (offsets 90, 91): see the finding

finding.title: Interface drift: BNK1CRA's copy of the DBCRFUN parameters is 40 bytes short (predicted defect)
finding.history: Commit afb4f68 (2026-07-23, 'CICS Account transaction history (#123)') added COMM-DESCRIPTION to PAYDBCR and updated DBCRFUN, XFRFUN, the API mappings and the Java caller; BNK1CRA, which declares the parameters inline instead of copying PAYDBCR, was not updated.
finding.predicted_effect: BNK1CRA passes 92 bytes; DBCRFUN addresses 132. DBCRFUN's success flag and fail code land past the end of BNK1CRA's parameter area, and BNK1CRA reads its flag from the bytes DBCRFUN treats as the start of the description. A refused debit would therefore likely be reported to the teller as 'Amount successfully applied' while the balance is unchanged. Static analysis only: to be confirmed on a running CICS system.
